chunks: Abu Hamza said: I have not heard of anyone among the people who was more ascetic than Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), except for what has reached me from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). Abu Hamza said: When Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would speak about ascetism and give admonition, he would make those in his presence weep.

Abu Hamza said: I read a parchment containing speech on ascetism from the words of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and I wrote down what was in it. Then I came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (may God's blessings be upon him), and I presented what was in it to him. He recognized it and corrected it. And what was in it was:

In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. May God suffice us and you from the scheming of the unjust, the aggression of the envious, and the violence of the tyrants. O believers! Do not let the tyrants and their followers — those who covet this world, who are inclined towards it, deceived by it, rushing towards it and towards its lifeless ruins and its chaff that will perish tomorrow — tempt you. Beware of what God has warned you about it, and practice abstinence from what God has told you to abstain from, and do not incline towards what is in this world as one who has taken it as a permanent abode and settled dwelling.

By God, that which is in it is evidence and warning for you — from the changing of its days, the reversal of its conditions, its punishments, and its mockery of its inhabitants. Truly it elevates the lowly and degrades the noble, and it will drive peoples into the Fire tomorrow. In this there is a lesson, a trial, and a deterrent for the wakeful. Truly the affairs that come upon you every day and night — the darknesses of strife, the occurrences of innovations, the traditions of oppression, the calamities of the age, the awe of rulers, and the whisperings of Satan — discourage hearts from awakening and distract them from finding guidance and recognizing the people of truth, except for the few whom God has protected. No one will understand the turns of its days, the changes of its conditions, and the harmful consequences of its strife, except one whom God protects, who has traveled the way of right guidance and followed the road of purpose.

No one understands the turns of its days, the shifts of its conditions, and the harmful consequences of its strife, except one whom God protects — who has traveled the way of right guidance and followed the road of purpose, then seeks help against that through ascetism, repeats reflection, takes heed through patience and is restrained, practices abstinence from the fleeting splendors of the world, turns away from its pleasures, desires the eternal bliss of the Hereafter and strives for it earnestly, watches over death, and detests life among the unjust people. He looks at what is in the world with a clear, sharp-sighted eye, and perceives the events of strife, the misguidance of innovations, and the injustice of tyrannical kings. By my life, you have turned your backs on the past matters during the bygone days — free of accumulated strife and the immersion in that which guides you toward avoiding the misguided.

...people of innovations, transgression, and corruption in the land without right. So seek help from God and return to obedience to God and obedience to the one most deserving of obedience among those who have been followed and obeyed. So beware, beware before regret and grief and presenting oneself before God and standing before Him. By God, no people have ever turned away from disobedience to God except toward His punishment, and no people have ever preferred the world over the Hereafter except that evil was their return and evil was their destination. And knowledge of God and deeds are nothing but two harmonious companions — whoever knows God fears Him, and fear drives him to act in obedience to God. And

And indeed the masters of knowledge and their followers who have known God, acted for Him, and desired Him — and God has said: 'Only those fear God, among His servants, who have knowledge' [Quran 35:28].

...from among His servants who have knowledge. So do not seek anything in this world through disobedience to God; occupy yourselves in this world with obedience to God; seize its days; strive for what will bring you salvation tomorrow from the punishment of God — for that is least in accountability, closest to excuse, and most hopeful for salvation. Give priority to the command of God and obedience to the one whose obedience God has made obligatory, before all other affairs. Do not give priority to the affairs that come to you from obedience to tyrants — the allurements of the world — over God, His obedience, and the obedience of the holders of authority among you. Know that you are servants of God, and we are with you. A Master and Ruler

...and Ruler will judge over us and over you tomorrow, and He is the One who will make you stand and question you. So prepare the answer before the standing, the questioning, and the presentation before the Lord of the Worlds — on that Day no soul will speak except by His permission. And know that God will not validate a liar on that Day, nor will He reject a truthful one, nor will He turn away the excuse of one who deserves it, nor excuse one without justification. He has the proof against His creation through the Messengers and the executors of authority after the Messengers. So fear God, servants of God, and embark on reforming yourselves and obeying God and obeying those whom He has appointed as guardians therein. Perhaps a remorseful one has repented for having neglected yesterday regarding the side of God and wasted from the rights of God. Seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him, for He accepts repentance, forgives sins, and knows what you do. And beware of the companionship of the disobedient, the assistance of the unjust, and the proximity of the corrupt. Be cautious of their strife and distance yourselves from their domain. Know that whoever opposes the guardians of God, follows a religion other than the religion of God, and acts independently without the command of God's guardian, will be in a blazing fire that consumes bodies from which their souls have departed and over which their misery has prevailed — they are dead, feeling no heat of the fire; but had they been alive, they would have experienced the pain of the fire's heat. Take lesson, O people of vision! Praise God for what He has guided you to, and know that you cannot escape from the power of God to another power. God and His Messenger will see your deeds, then you will be gathered to Him. So benefit from admonition and educate yourselves with the conduct of the righteous.

key_terms.أُولُو الْأَمْرِ: Holders of authority; in Shia interpretation, the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الزُّهَّاد: Those who practice ascetism, the ascetics
key_terms.الزُّهْد: Ascetism, renunciation of worldly attachments in favor of the Hereafter
key_terms.الطَّوَاغِيت: Tyrants, false gods; those who exceed proper limits in oppression and usurp authority
key_terms.الْبِدَع: Innovations (in religion), deviations from the established path
key_terms.الْفِتَن: Trials, strife, civil discord and tribulations
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Peace be upon him; honorific used for Prophets and Imams
key_terms.وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ: The guardian/authority of God; the Imam as divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin teach about ascetism and avoiding the temptations of the world?
ai.summary: This is a profound exhortatory sermon transmitted by Abu Hamza al-Thumali, containing Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin's (as) parchment on ascetism (zuhd). Written during the Umayyad era when the Shia faced severe political oppression, the Imam admonishes the faithful to beware of tyrants and the allures of the dunya, to practice zuhd, to follow the legitimate authority of the Imams (Ulu al-Amr), and to prepare for the reckoning before God. The parchment quotes Quran 35:28 to establish that only true scholars — those who truly know God — genuinely fear Him and act accordingly.
